plates.title: Mac Pro 1,1 — physical bay map
plates.purpose: Where the boot SSD and the three 1 TB HDDs physically sit, and how they reach the PCIe RAID card.
plates.view: three-quarter cutaway of the tower with the side panel removed

nodes.detail: 2006 Mac Pro tower, A1186, aluminium cheese-grater front, handles top and bottom, side panel released by the rear lever.
5.25in optical bay 1 — slot-load SuperDrive on PATA / ATA-100, not SATA.
5.25in optical bay 2 — empty; ATA-100 cabling with 4-pin Molex power.

Bay 1 - Lion SSD Base - 1 TB 2.5in SATA SSD loaded INSIDE the top sled of the four-bay cage, sled latch and captive thumbscrews visible, flush within the bay opening and not resting on top of the cage - boot 10.6.8, Lion 10.7 destination - NEVER ERASE.
Bay 2 — 1 TB 3.5in HDD — RAID 5 member 0 — cabled to the PCIe RAID controller.
Bay 3 — 1 TB 3.5in HDD — RAID 5 member 1 — replaces the Crucial MX500 'start disk clone' (Lion install target; do not wipe until Lion boots from the SSD).
Bay 4 — 1 TB 3.5in HDD — RAID 5 member 2 — replaces 'Mac OS X Install ESD'.
Slot 1 double-wide x16 = GPU. Slots 2/3/4 are full-length and reconfigurable; stock allocation 16/4/4/1. The RAID card goes in an x4 slot.
Four-port SATA/SAS RAID controller seated in PCIe slot 4: metal rear bracket on the chassis edge, gold fingers inside the slot, one SFF-8087 port. Slot bank numbered 1 to 4, card in slot 4.
SFF-8087 to 4x SATA breakout (MaxConnect-style SAS/SATA link) routes the bay drives to the card. The four logic-board bay SATA ports stay unused; direct-attach is bypassed.
Legend field: exactly four rows in bay order - one SSD icon for bay 1 and three HDD icons for bays 2, 3 and 4. No other drive icons anywhere in the plate.
Mac Pro 1,1 · A1186 · 2006 · 51.1 x 20.6 x 47.5 cm · 19.2 kg · four cable-free direct-attach 3.5in bays at 3 Gb/s · six SATA ports (4 bays + 2 spare) · PATA optical bays.

renderNotes: ABSOLUTE TEXT RULE: any string not present in the SHORT LABEL list is a defect. Words that appear only as drawing descriptions (brushed aluminium, Mac OS X internal, tower, cold vault, parity) must NEVER be rendered as captions.
Every drive icon lives either inside the Mac Pro bays or in the single legend column. No loose floating drive icons in the honeycomb field.
The bay 1 boot SSD has NO cable at all: it is joined to the legend only. Only bays 2, 3 and 4 get leads, and every one of those leads terminates at the RAID card.
Draw the slot bank numerals as 1, 2, 3, 4 - four separate digits, evenly spaced, no gaps.

plates.title: AppleRAID-free path — hardware RAID 5 map for BTC cold storage
plates.purpose: How three 1 TB members become one 2 TB vault, and what the vault is and is not.

nodes.detail: Mac Pro 1,1 · boot SSD on the logic board + three 1 TB HDDs as a hardware RAID 5 set on a PCIe controller.
Lion SSD Base — 1 TB 2.5in SATA SSD — boot volume 10.6.8 to 10.7 — Mac OS Extended (Journaled), GUID — DELIBERATELY NOT a member of the RAID set.
Member 0 — Bay 2 — 1 TB 3.5in HDD — 3 Gb/s — channel 1 of the RAID controller.
Member 1 — Bay 3 — 1 TB 3.5in HDD — 3 Gb/s — channel 2 of the RAID controller.
Member 2 — Bay 4 — 1 TB 3.5in HDD — 3 Gb/s — channel 3 of the RAID controller.

Distributed parity striping across three members: 3 TB raw becomes 2 TB usable ((n-1) x member), survives the loss of any one member, rebuilds onto a replacement drive. Not expressible in Disk Utility — AppleRAID is stripe/mirror/concat only.
2 TB usable — Mac OS Extended (Journaled), GUID partition map — mount point /Volumes/BTCColdVault — exported and unmounted when not in use, no auto-mount at login.
Capacity plan: ~700 GB Bitcoin full chain (2026, still growing) + chainstate + wallet + headroom inside 2 TB usable. A pruned node needs only a few GB.

RAID 5 is redundancy, not backup. A rebuild reads 2 TB: about a 15% chance of an unrecoverable read error on 1e14-rated consumer drives, about 1.5% on 1e15 enterprise drives. Seeds and keys stay offline on paper or steel, never on this array.
Volume format Mac OS Extended (Journaled) on GUID — APFS is not mountable by 10.7. Every drive is SATA 3 Gb/s; the PCIe 1.0 x4 uplink is about 1 GB/s and is not the bottleneck for three HDDs.
Three HDD channels pass through the PCIe 1.0 x4 RAID controller in slot 4, about 1 GB/s uplink.

renderNotes: ABSOLUTE TEXT RULE: any string not present in the SHORT LABEL list is a defect. Do not caption the host silhouette, the members or the volume with descriptive words.
All member, engine, volume, SSD and warning panels are the SAME flat-top hexagon - no octagons, no chamfered squares.
The footer strip HFS+J - GUID - 3 Gb/s sits inside its own wide hexagon panel, not as floating text.

plates.title: PCIe slot allocation and cable routing
plates.purpose: Which slot the RAID card takes, what it costs in lanes, and how the bay drives get cabled to it.
plates.view: rear slot area of the logic board with the drive stack beside it

nodes.detail: Four PCIe 1.0 slots on the Mac Pro 1,1 logic board; stock lane allocation 16/4/4/1, reconfigurable with the Expansion Slot Utility.
Slot 1 — double-wide 16-lane — graphics card stays here.
Slot 2 — one lane in the stock allocation — too narrow for a RAID card.
Slot 3 — four lanes — usable alternative for the RAID card.
Slot 4 — four lanes at 2.5 GT/s (PCIe 1.0) — RAID card lives here; about 1 GB/s uplink, far above what three HDDs can push.
4-port SATA/SAS controller with one SFF-8087 connector, RAID 0/1/3/5/6/10, 256 MB cache, Intel IOP-class RAID processor.
One SFF-8087 to four SATA breakout — three leads run to bays 2, 3 and 4, one spare lead is left capped.
Bays 2, 3 and 4 — three 1 TB 3.5in HDDs on their sleds. The logic-board bay SATA ports are left unpopulated while the breakout is in use.
MacPro1,1 has 32-bit EFI, so an Option ROM that is 64-bit only will not boot from the card. That is fine here: the array is a data vault, the system boots from the Bay 1 SSD.

renderNotes: Every panel, including the four slot panels and the footer plate, is a regular flat-top hexagon of the same proportions; no pill shapes, no long chamfered bars.
Do not render the word CAUTION or any chip label; the amber footer hexagon carries only EFI32 - NO BOOT.
Draw a double-wide graphics card seated in SLOT 1, occupying that hexagon, so slot 1 is visibly taken.
